key_insight: Quantum representations become useful computational methods only when input access, measurement, and decoding support the desired estimate or decision.
engineering_relevance: Imaging engineers must evaluate end-to-end resources and output requirements rather than infer computational advantage from compact quantum encodings.
method: Distinguish amplitude encoding of input values from encoding complete candidate labelings.
Use complementary measurements for unknown-phase inference and matrix SVD to explain pure-state entanglement.
Translate a four-pixel segmentation objective into a cost operator and a QAOA sampling circuit.
evidence_signal: In the four-pixel example, one QAOA layer reduces mean energy from 1.675 to 0.686 versus uniform sampling, but a nonoptimal labeling is more probable than the optimum (0.484 versus 0.365); archived IBM and IQM measurements illustrate a separate six-variable boundary decision.
watch_item: Amplitude storage does not enable full-array readout, and lower mean energy does not guarantee that the optimal solution is sampled most often.
paper_title: Quantum Computing through Computational Imaging: Representations, Measurement, and Inference
